newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus jails two Israelis for staging escape.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus jails two Israelis for staging escape.

text.p: Two Israelis were jailed for four years on Wednesday for waylaying a Cypriot police car in the centre of Nicosia to free two of their countrymen in September.
David Biton, 24, and Amor Shimon, 28, from Haifa gasped when the sentence for orchestrating the short-lived escape of the prisoners to Turkish-held northern Cyprus was passed.
But their Cypriot lawyer Phoivos Clerides told Reuters: "I thought the prison sentence was quite reasonable."

A third defendant Shuki Samana, 24 -- one of the escapees -- was given a nine-month jail sentence, suspended for three years, for escaping custody. The other prisoner freed, Biton's brother Avi, 21, had appeared in court last month.

Biton and Shimon pleaded guilty to holding up the police car on a busy street in central Nicosia in mid-September. All four escaped to the north of the island, but Turkish Cypriot police returned them the same day.

Samana and Avi Biton had been in custody on suspicion of distributing forged $100 bills. Police were taking the two from the island's central prisons in Nicosia to the coastal town of Larnaca when the unescorted vehicle was intercepted.

The court dismissed a defence submission that severe lapses in police security tempted the defendants, but added that their confession, family circumstances and cooperation with police were mitigating factors.
David Biton and Shimon released the two prisoners from the police car, put them on the back of high-powered motorcycles and roared through a United Nations checkpoint to northern Cyprus.

Avi Biton did not appear before the court, which last month jailed him for two-and-a-half years for possession and distribution of 72 forged $100 bills in August. The earlier verdict took into account the escape.
Samana is due to reappear in court next Monday in connection with the forgery case. Defence lawyers said prosecutors are to withdraw the charges.
